about: Which content key a sealed contact name needs (wappie DS50). A batch
envelope is a header of 8 bytes ("WS", version 1, suite 1, mode 2 for
batch, a u16 big-endian epoch, one reserved byte), then the content key's
id as a u32 big-endian, the nonce and the ciphertext. Only that key opens
it. key_id is the id a reader opens the name with; null means the envelope
names no usable key (not a batch envelope, too short, or an id outside 1
to 2147483647, which a keys request would refuse), and a reader takes the
server's per-name id, then the row's content_key_id.
Sealed by internal/crypto/seal under a throwaway archive key; the
invalid ones are a valid one with bytes changed. Read by internal/store's
TestContactNameKeyIDVectors and by wappie-cloud's web tests from the core

vectors.name: business name under content key 2147483647, the largest id
full name under content key 65536 (the id's bytes 00 01 00 00)
batch envelope naming content key 2147483648, above any stored id
the header and three bytes of the id
